Geography 2007-I.question: Among the following forest types in India, which one occupies the largest area?
Geography 2007-I.explanation: (b)  The Moist deciduous forests are more pronounced in the regions which record rainfall between 100-200cm. These forests are found in the northeastern states along the foothills of Himalayas, easteren slopes of the Western Ghats and Odisha. Tropical moist deciduous forest covers arounds 37% of the total cover in India which is the largest occupied area among 16 different forest types of the country.
